name: Arcade daily solo and async skill challenges
user: Casual players who enjoy a short challenge and optionally buy visual customization.
first_result: Finish one solvable daily skill game and compare a shareable result.
loop: Return for a different board or a friend's challenge
return_trigger: Fresh daily boards and improvement are plausible return occasions; actual repeat play is unmeasured.
paid_value: Optional cosmetic identity; cosmetics do not establish a recurring subscription benefit.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: cosmetic purchases equivalent to US$2–5 through Telegram Stars; final Stars amount and payout remain unverified. Zero subscription MRR. Subscription conversion requires an explicit change to existing cosmetic-only policy.
pricing.free: Complete games without ads or paid advantages
pricing.paid: Optional cosmetic themes

dependencies: Telegram Stars eligibility for intended seller
compute: Local deterministic puzzles; bounded seed delivery and optional score verification. No generative inference required.
content_burden: Maintain solvability, difficulty and original language pools; do not count machine translations as editorial acceptance.
first_scope: Async result link that works without an installed app
acquisition: Demonstrate a playable daily board and measure whether result recipients actually finish a round; unverified.

competitors.name: Puzzmo
competitors.facts: Daily puzzle collection with paid Plus access.
competitors.price: US App Store lists Puzzmo Plus monthly at USD3.99; another Plus SKU is USD39.99 but its term is not labeled in the IAP list.

competitors.name: Puzz.com
competitors.facts: Free daily solo puzzles and optional unlimited/ad-free premium.
competitors.price: Plus displayed $1.99/month or $19.99/year; ISO dollar currency not specified.

difference: A restrained, multilingual, no-ad daily experience with cosmetic-only purchases; differentiation and acquisition remain unvalidated.
risk: Free competitors already supply daily variety; attractive play can generate no meaningful cosmetic revenue.
experiment: Observe unaided round completion, independent return on different days, recipient play from shared results, and a real cosmetic purchase.
stop_rule: Do not expand the roster if returning players ignore cosmetics or sharing brings no subsequent play.
overlap: Keep party decks in Hijinx; consolidate all short solo puzzle themes here. Do not count each game as a product.
rationale: Immediate value and independent play are strong; code reuse reduces experiment effort, not demand uncertainty. Cosmetics constrain paid value.

name: Interactive detective casebook
user: Solo mystery fans purchasing complete original cases.
first_result: Inspect evidence, form a defensible accusation and see how the clues support the solution.
loop: Resolve the accusation with an explanation
return_trigger: A new authored mystery; returning for another case is plausible, not measured.
paid_value: New fair-play mysteries with satisfying solutions; sell complete cases before promising a subscription cadence.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD5–10 per complete case. Pack sales contribute zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Additional standalone cases

compute: Local branching state and evidence graph; static media with download-size limits.
content_burden: Every case needs coherent suspects, clues, alternative hypotheses and tested solutions; creative labor dominates.
first_scope: Complete case with replayable solution review
acquisition: A spoiler-free playable opening and deduction clip aimed at mystery-game audiences; unverified.

competitors.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami
competitors.facts: Developer listing describes a short single-player mystery using interviews, evidence and fill-in deductions.
competitors.price: Opened storefront displayed PLN35.99 for the base game.

competitors.name: The Case of the Golden Idol
competitors.facts: Publisher storefront for a single-player deduction game.
competitors.price: not verified

difference: A compact browser case designed around explaining an accusation instead of hidden-object tapping; incumbent absence is not claimed.
risk: Case quality and original writing, not software, decide value; each successful case creates another production obligation.
experiment: Let players solve without facilitation, offer a second case on another day, and test a real case purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if players need author intervention to reach a fair solution or finish the free case without wanting another.
overlap: Separate from E053 spatial escape puzzles and E054 choice-driven stories. Not a party role-playing deck for Hijinx.
rationale: Clear complete outcome and demonstrability; content production limits cadence and pack purchases are not MRR.

name: Solo escape-room adventures
user: Players wanting a complete spatial puzzle adventure on a phone or browser.
first_result: Manipulate objects and mechanisms to escape one self-contained room.
return_trigger: New rooms and mastery of puzzle mechanics; repeat purchase is unverified.
paid_value: Complete additional room chapters with original art and fair hints.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD4–8 per chapter; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Additional room chapters

compute: Local 2D interaction engine; bundled assets and bounded downloads.
content_burden: Mechanism design, art, hints and testing every state to prevent unwinnable sequences.
acquisition: A short interactive mechanism in a playable browser demo; unverified.

competitors.name: Rusty Lake
competitors.facts: Studio offers Cube Escape point-and-click adventures and separate premium narrative games.
competitors.price: Free and premium products described; exact premium prices not verified.

difference: Short, accessible tactile puzzles with explicit recovery from mistakes; no claim this is absent elsewhere.
risk: Polished free escape games set a high content standard; new rooms require continuous design work.
experiment: Observe unaided escape, voluntary second-room play on another occasion and a chapter purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if hints replace deduction or returning players prefer free alternatives over the paid chapter.
overlap: E052 centers evidence and accusation; this centers spatial manipulation. All room themes consolidate here.
rationale: Simple activation but significant art/state testing and weak differentiation in an established game genre.

name: Branching interactive fiction library
user: Readers buying stories in which their decisions change characters and outcomes.
first_result: Finish a short episode with meaningful consequences and a complete emotional beat.
loop: Return for the next episode or another route
return_trigger: Story continuation and alternate routes; habitual use remains a hypothesis.
paid_value: Edited original stories with substantive branching and complete arcs.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD6–12 per finished volume; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Full story volumes

compute: Local story-state engine; no live LLM required.
content_burden: High: original writing, meaningful branches, endings and continuity QA.
acquisition: Share a compelling first decision and playable chapter with fiction readers; unverified.

competitors.name: Choice of Games
competitors.facts: Publisher describes text-based interactive novels on mobile and web, using its ChoiceScript language.
competitors.price: not verified

difference: A short-volume library with transparent completion length and no per-choice currency; distinction unvalidated.
risk: The scarce input is memorable writing; a generic AI story wrapper provides little reason to pay.
experiment: Test unaided episode completion, return for an unresolved character arc, and a full-volume purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if readers skip prose to outcomes or show no desire to continue a specific story.
overlap: Reading a finished narrative, not creative-lane story-authoring tools or E055 open-ended tabletop play.
rationale: Independent delivery is easy; sustaining differentiated story quality is harder than the engine.

name: Solo tabletop adventure companion
user: Tabletop role-playing fans wanting a coherent solo session without recruiting a game master.
first_result: Create a character, resolve a scene and save a concrete adventure consequence.
return_trigger: The next scene in a continuing personal campaign; repeat use unmeasured.
paid_value: Reviewed adventure modules, reliable rules handling and persistent campaign continuity.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Growing module library and multiple campaigns

compute: Local rules and random tables first; any optional generated prose metered separately with hard caps.
content_burden: Scenario writing, encounter balance and consistent state transitions; do not promise arbitrary rules compatibility.
first_scope: Oracle prompts plus complete starter quest
acquisition: Show a complete solo encounter from start to consequence to solo-RPG audiences; unverified.

competitors.name: Mythic Game Master Emulator Second Edition
competitors.facts: Official publisher describes oracle-based solo play usable alone or with other RPG systems.
competitors.price: GBP38 for the physical hardback shown; digital-only price not verified.

difference: A bounded digital campaign that keeps rules and consequences consistent without a live human or unrestricted chat.
risk: Dedicated solo players may prefer a book and notebook; automation can remove the improvisation they enjoy.
experiment: Observe a complete unaided encounter, independent campaign resumption and actual library subscription purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if players abandon saved campaigns or repeatedly bypass the app to resolve ordinary moves.
overlap: Different from branching fiction: persistent character rules and player-authored decisions, not fixed narrative routes.
rationale: Strong independent-session proposition; onboarding and specialized content reduce speed and confidence.

name: Chess mistake-to-practice coach
user: Amateur chess players willing to pay for practice based on their own recurring mistakes.
first_result: Import a PGN, understand one turning point and solve a related corrective exercise.
loop: Test the skill in the next game
return_trigger: Each played game supplies new practice evidence; use and improvement are unverified.
paid_value: Accurate longitudinal diagnosis and focused exercises beyond raw engine lines.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Bounded game analysis and evolving practice plan

compute: Local engine where possible; cap server analysis by games, depth and CPU time.
content_burden: Reviewed explanations and exercise families; avoid ungrounded LLM claims about best moves.
acquisition: Publish an interactive before/after example from an authorized game; unverified.

competitors.name: Aimchess
competitors.facts: Analyzes games and builds personalized lessons, recurring-mistake exercises and weekly plans.
competitors.price: Displayed $7.99 monthly or $57.99 annually; ISO dollar currency not specified.

difference: A deliberately narrow error-to-drill experience with inspectable engine evidence; not an asserted missing incumbent feature.
risk: Aimchess already expresses the core proposition, while free chess platforms provide substantial analysis.
experiment: Observe PGN-to-exercise completion, new-game return and payment for sustained individualized practice.
stop_rule: Stop if players cannot identify a useful distinction from their existing free analysis or Aimchess.
overlap: Hobby-specific feedback, not Arcade puzzle entertainment or broad educational curriculum.
rationale: Strong recurring input and established paid alternative; direct overlap makes differentiation weak.

name: Board-game learn-and-reference companion
user: Board-game owners learning a supported game and resolving rules during play.
first_result: Complete an interactive first-turn tutorial and find a rule without reading the entire manual.
loop: Return when replaying or learning another supported game
return_trigger: Board-game sessions and new purchases; cadence is user-dependent.
paid_value: Accurate interactive tutorials and fast authoritative rules references across supported games.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Maintained tutorial library and saved references

dependencies: Publisher permissions or appropriate rule-content rights
compute: Curated/local search and decision trees; no live reasoning required.
content_burden: Every supported edition and expansion requires rule verification and errata maintenance.
first_scope: Searchable rule examples with source references
acquisition: Demonstrate setup-to-first-turn beside an existing game; unverified.

competitors.name: Dized
competitors.facts: Provides board-game tutorials, rules, optional tools and game-specific extras.
competitors.price: Displayed $3/month or $30/year; ISO dollar currency not specified.

difference: Edition-specific authoritative answers surfaced in the current turn; hypothesis, not claimed market whitespace.
risk: Dized already offers free tutorials; obtaining broad rights and accurate coverage can dominate cost.
experiment: Test unaided first play, rule lookup on a later session and subscription purchase for another game.
stop_rule: Stop if supported-game breadth is required before users pay or rights costs exceed a bounded pilot.
overlap: Physical-board-game reference, not Hijinx original party games or complete digital games.
rationale: Clear job but external rights, specialist content and established free coverage weaken independence.

name: Trading-card collection and price notebook
user: Active card collectors tracking variants, acquisition cost and collection changes.
first_result: Identify a card, place it in the correct set and see a sourced market reference.
loop: See set completion and price changes
Return after collecting or market updates
return_trigger: Acquisitions, trades and new releases; market attention is not proven paid retention.
paid_value: Accurate variant matching, collection history and licensed price comparisons.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Larger collections, history and bounded scans

dependencies: Licensed card catalog and market data
compute: Bounded scans with manual confirmation; cache licensed data and cap image processing.
content_burden: Catalog releases, variants and price provenance; do not represent estimates as appraisals.
first_scope: Set checklist and sourced price history
acquisition: Demonstrate a mistaken variant corrected in one scan; unverified.

competitors.name: Collectr
competitors.facts: Offers card scanning, collection tracking, market history and export.
competitors.price: Displayed $7.99 if billed monthly or $4.99/month billed annually; annual checkout total and ISO currency not verified.

difference: Provenance-first variant confirmation for a narrow supported franchise; unvalidated against established tools.
risk: Collectors may require broad reliable market data before switching; data licensing can dominate the business.
experiment: Test unaided correct-card entry, subsequent acquisition logging and paid history/scan use.
stop_rule: Stop if data rights are unavailable or variant corrections require manual staff intervention.
overlap: Distinct from E070 coin attribution: contemporary release variants and dynamic card markets, not historical object cataloguing.
rationale: Strong visible utility and recurring collections; licensed data and exact variants reduce feasibility.

name: Book taste discovery and private reading journal
user: Frequent leisure readers choosing their next book and retaining personal reactions.
first_result: Find a plausible next book from mood and previous likes, then save a private reading note.
loop: Pick a book from a small explained shortlist
return_trigger: Finishing or abandoning a book; slower than daily media use.
paid_value: Reliable personal taste memory and useful discovery without requiring a social network.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Deeper taste exploration and reading-pattern tools

compute: Catalog search and local preference matching; cap optional recommendation inference.
content_burden: Accurate metadata, spoiler control and interpretable mood taxonomy.
acquisition: An interactive 'what should I read tonight?' example for one reading community; unverified.

competitors.name: The StoryGraph
competitors.facts: Combines mood-based discovery, statistics, private journal, reading queue and an optional Plus plan.
competitors.price: Mostly free; Plus price not verified.

difference: Explainable small recommendations anchored in private reactions; the incumbent already overlaps materially.
risk: Strong free products already deliver tracking and recommendations; a diary may not justify payment.
experiment: Test a recommendation actually started, return after reading and a premium discovery purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if readers save suggestions but do not start books or cannot name paid value beyond free alternatives.
overlap: Leisure selection and memory, not learning-lane comprehension or creative writing.
rationale: Low-friction independent utility but weak payment boundary and crowded direct alternatives.

name: Art discovery and visual literacy
user: Curious adults who want to notice and understand art without visiting a museum.
first_result: Inspect one artwork, notice a prompted detail and compare an initial interpretation with a reviewed explanation.
loop: Look closely at one rights-cleared artwork
Find and explain a visual detail
Compare interpretations or a related work
Revisit the theme in a later artwork
return_trigger: A short daily or weekly artwork encounter and returning themes; habit and retention remain unverified.
paid_value: Authored guided-looking sequences, comparisons and revisits that build observation skills beyond reading a daily art fact.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay. Test finite themed packs instead if users value completion but not continuing releases; packs produce zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: One complete guided-looking sequence and a small sample theme
pricing.paid: Continuing reviewed theme sequences, comparison exercises and a personal observation archive

dependencies: Rights-cleared or verified public-domain artwork images
Qualified art-history and visual-literacy editorial review
compute: Curated images and deterministic interactions; compressed image delivery with bounded offline cache; no live image-generation or unrestricted interpretation model.
content_burden: Substantial original guided-looking prompts, accurate context, comparative artwork selection, accessibility descriptions and image-rights checks. Human editorial work continues with each theme.
first_scope: One complete themed sequence using rights-cleared works
Later revisit that transfers the same observation skill
acquisition: Show one surprising detail reveal followed by an independent comparison task; use the complete free sequence as the demonstration. Distribution is untested.

competitors.name: DailyArt
competitors.facts: Official site offers a free daily artwork with a short story, thematic collections and a wider archive. Its FAQ describes art-historian authorship and public-domain or licensed images.
competitors.price: Daily artwork offer explicitly free; current paid subscription amount not verified.

competitors.name: Google Arts & Culture
competitors.facts: Public site provides artwork exploration, themed collections, related-work comparisons and close-looking detail explanations without requiring a physical visit.
competitors.price: Opened public content accessible without payment; no paid price verified.

difference: Practice noticing details and comparing interpretations before reading a reviewed explanation, then revisit the skill in another artwork. This interaction emphasis is unvalidated and does not assert competitors lack it.
risk: Free DailyArt and Google Arts & Culture already provide compelling discovery and close-looking content. A polished daily card could retain readers without generating payment, while accurate authored sequences and image rights create continuing costs.
experiment: Observe an unaided artwork encounter, a later comparison using the same skill, an independent return to another theme, then actual payment for the proposed continuation.
stop_rule: Stop if participants only enjoy the free reveal, fail to transfer observations to another work, or prefer free alternatives to paid guided sequences.
overlap: Replaces E060 film-journal duplicate of E059. This is remote art appreciation rather than a local museum directory, creative drawing instruction, general history curriculum, or a location-dependent museum guide.
rationale: A complete first encounter is quick, visual and self-contained. Ongoing paid value and distinction remain weak against free authored alternatives, while specialist content production limits feasibility.

name: Video-game backlog and next-session picker
user: Players with purchased games who struggle to choose and finish one.
first_result: Select a realistic game for tonight and preserve a resume note.
loop: Enter owned games and session time
Save progress and a next-action note
return_trigger: Each gaming session and purchase; sustained logging is unverified.
paid_value: Useful resume memory and collection planning; library size alone is not a premium benefit.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD15 lifetime desktop/web license; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Unlimited local collection and advanced planning

dependencies: Manual entry or standard user-export import
compute: Local collection, preference filters and small optional metadata cache.
content_burden: Metadata quality and platform editions; avoid maintaining mandatory proprietary account integrations.
acquisition: Show a large backlog becoming one playable evening plan; unverified.

competitors.name: GG
competitors.facts: Official site describes game discovery, collection tracking and seeing friends' games.
competitors.price: not verified

difference: Focus on resuming owned games and deliberate completion instead of collecting another wishlist.
risk: A list and console's recent-games screen may solve enough of the problem for free.
experiment: Observe a chosen session, later reuse of its resume note and a one-time upgrade purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if users organize once and never use the session picker or resume note again.
overlap: Gaming organization rather than E060 passive film discovery or E068 performance coaching.
rationale: Easy to demonstrate and build locally; recurring administration and payment need proof.

name: Birdwatching field journal and identification companion
user: Recreational birdwatchers recording observations and learning to recognize local birds.

loop: Return for another outing and seasonal target
return_trigger: Birding outings and seasonal changes; geography affects frequency.
paid_value: Personal expedition history and advanced organization, not basic identification already free elsewhere.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.paid: Trip organization, backup and longitudinal field analysis

compute: Local journal; bounded optional photo/audio inference with explicit uncertainty.
content_burden: Regional species coverage, identification cues and taxonomy updates.
acquisition: Demonstrate one observation becoming a verifiable journal entry; unverified.

competitors.name: Merlin Bird ID
competitors.facts: Cornell offers offline sound/photo identification, life lists and location-season bird lists.
competitors.price: Free.

difference: An evidence-oriented outing journal; do not claim superior identification or infer access to Merlin's data.
risk: A trusted free incumbent already combines most of the core experience with far richer data.
experiment: Test unaided sighting logging, another outing and payment for organization beyond free identification.
stop_rule: Stop if users value identification alone or cannot distinguish the journal from their existing free tools.
overlap: Wildlife field hobby, not pet care, science curriculum or E063 night-sky observing.
rationale: Visible delight and repeat outings; free comprehensive competition sharply weakens the paid proposition.

paid_value: Maintained observing plans and personal progress tailored to available equipment.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: Tonight's basic sky and one target
pricing.paid: Curated observing programs, event calendar and journal

compute: Local sky calculations; cache catalogs and cap weather-provider requests.
content_burden: Reviewed observing instructions, visibility constraints and event calendars.
acquisition: A shareable 'find this tonight' demonstration for one visible event; unverified.

competitors.name: Stellarium Mobile and Plus

rationale: Immediate visible outcome when conditions cooperate; incumbent overlap and weather constrain recurring value.
